newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX noon Nikkei languishes, shrugs off FOMC.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX noon Nikkei languishes, shrugs off FOMC.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures were a shade lower at around midday on Thursday, reflecting thin interest in the Japanese stock market, dealers said.
After trading within a 170-point range, the September Nikkei futures eased 10 points to 20,200 at 0300GMT. Volume was light, at 5,530 lots.
Dealers said the market shrugged off the two-day Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which ended on Wednesday, with interest rates unchanged.
"As expected the FOMC left the interest rates unchanged. People was now watching for the U.S. non-farm payrolls later tonight," said a dealer with a Japanese house.

Market expectations are for a strong set of June U.S. employment data. According to a Reuters poll, June employment is expected to rise 222,000 after a 138,000 gain in May. But many are forecasting as high as 300,000.
Dealers said an annual meeting of bankers from 0500 GMT on Thursday, where Bank of Japan's governor Yasuo Matsushita is scheduled to address, was also keeping activity at bay.
